newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa Cargo silent on fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo silent on fuel surcharge.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it did not wish to say at present whether it might drop its air cargo fuel surcharge.
A Lufthansa Cargo spokeswoman said only: "We will make a statement on this question in the near future."
The cautious reaction followed the announcement by Delta Air Lines yesterday that it was ending a 10 US cents per kg surcharge on freight between the US and Europe/Asia with immediate effect.
The US carrier's regional director cargo sales & service Europe, Danita Waterfall, justified the move with "a significant decrease" in fuel prices in recent weeks.
British Airways and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines have both said they were studying the situation but it could not yet say whether they would drop their surcharge.
Lufthansa Cargo was the first airline to introduce a cargo fuel surcharge last year when it applied a 15 pfennigs, or 10 US cents, per kg surcharge from November 1.
